page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor. The CPU architecture includes a 128 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1d cache per core, with single-threaded execution per core. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 1890 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25% tier. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient; the Passmark memory score and large-block uncached memory read/write bandwidths (450.77 GB/sec read and 169.21 GB/sec write) rank in the top 10% tier. Database operations also perform in the top 10% tier, supported by strong Redis SET operations at 61.98 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 53.68 GB/sec. However, large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10% tier.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D32plds_v6 represents a compute-optimized profile with a low-memory footprint. The inclusion of 1890 GB of local storage and high-speed memory bandwidth provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high-speed local data access without the overhead of external storage. This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, web serving, and software compilation, whereas it is less optimal for memory-intensive applications or large-scale AI model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is a compute-optimized, ARM-based virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated physical cores powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and 1890 GB of local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong multi-core CPU performance and top-tier memory bandwidth, with uncached large-block reads reaching 450.77 GB/sec. Benchmark results highlight exceptional database operation speeds and high static web serving throughput, placing it in the top 10% and top 25% tiers respectively. Conversely, its low memory-to-core ratio and poor large-model LLM prompt processing performance make it less suitable for memory-heavy or massive AI workloads. It is highly effective for multi-threaded tasks, web serving, and local database operations.
